description: Pirouette initiation rate against dC/dt 4 s earlier, digitised from Pierce-Shimomura, Morse & Lockery (1999), J Neurosci 19(21):9557-9569, Figure 8 (the black curves, smoothed by the authors with a 4001-point box filter). The reference for the dC/dt quintile ratio.

source.citation: Pierce-Shimomura JT, Morse TM, Lockery SR (1999). The fundamental role of pirouettes in Caenorhabditis elegans chemotaxis. J Neurosci 19(21):9557-9569. doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.19-21-09557.1999; PMC6782915.
source.figure: Figure 8A (biotin gradient, 32,458 points) and 8B (NH4Cl gradient, 29,171 points), page 9564
source.copyright: (c) 1999 Society for Neuroscience. The PDF is not vendored; only values read from the figure are, with the citation.

method: Page 8 rendered at 500 dpi with PyMuPDF. Axes calibrated from the tick marks' pixel positions (rate 0 to 0.14 s^-1 on the left axis; dC/dt ticks at -0.2/-0.1/0/0.1 in A and -0.1/0/0.1 in B, fitted linearly). At each listed dC/dt, every thin black stroke in that pixel column was listed as a rate; the authors' dashed spontaneous-rate line (0.029-0.0297) and their black point-count histogram (lowest strokes) were set aside and the remaining stroke read as the curve. Where the curve crosses the dashed line or falls steeply (A near 0; B near -0.005) the stroke is thickened and its centre is read. Reading error is about half a stroke width, +/-0.0007 s^-1. Script: scripts/analysis/pierce_shimomura_digitise.py (needs the PDF, downloaded by browser).
calibration_check: The dashed line reads 0.029-0.0297 s^-1 in both panels; the paper's text gives the spontaneous rate in a uniform concentration as r = 0.0296 +/- 0.00213 s^-1 (n = 47).

reference_ratio.rule: the curve's rate at its most negative digitised dC/dt over its rate at its most positive, the figure's extreme bins standing for the worm's extreme dC/dt quintiles (ranks only; the figure's dC/dt axis is not mapped onto a simulated worm's)

beside: Lee 2026 (bioRxiv) is cited for 0.533 -> 0.056 s^-1, a ratio of 9.5, about four times the digitised ratios; its units and measure were not checked, and it is not the reference.
